note: The rendered check's rows and the sabotages that prove each one sees (#597, #807). Read by browser-checks/rendered_features.mjs, which runs the rows, and by browser-checks/lib/sabotage.py, which breaks a copy of the site one way at a time. Both platforms call the same two files, so the rows live here once. Deliberately NOT in contracts/: nothing here is a sentence a teacher reads or a rule the product follows; it is a test both platforms run (the #597 plan, section 4). The product rule that a site asks nothing of any other host becomes a contract with #566.

thirdPartyHostsToday.pinnedWhy: Each host to the pages that may ask it and the paths it may be asked for (597b review finding 2, measured 2026-11-13 in both engines): a listed host asked from another page or for another path fails the own-host row everywhere, and a pinned page that ran without asking its host fails it on a deployed site, so the pins shrink with #566. expectedLinesPerEngine is what a deployed run's EXPECTED lines must number in each engine (one per listed host); verify-deploy.sh compares each host's count with it, so a list that grew or shrank without this number moving is a failure.
thirdPartyHostsToday.why: What a built site asks of other hosts on Quartz 4.5.0 (measured 2026-11-13 on every fixture page, both engines): the theme's Google Fonts stylesheet and its faces, and Mermaid's engine from cdnjs on a page with a diagram. #566 empties this list. A request to any other host fails the own-host row, so a NEW third party is red already. On this Mac (--site) these hosts are allowed, a subset (plan review M3). On a deployed site (--base) no request may leave the site's own host (the owner, 2026-11-13), so each of them is an EXPECTED FAILURE of the own-host row there: printed as an EXPECTED line and counted, never a pass; and a host on this list that no page asked for in an engine's whole run is a FAILURE that says to take it off, so the list shrinks with #566 and the gate tightens (browser-checks/lib/expected_failures.mjs, #597's second half).

expectedConsole.why: Netlify injects its ad badge into every page; the site's policy refuses its script inside an about:srcdoc frame, by design, 700 to 850 ms after first paint, in both engines (settled on #625; documentation/07, Suppressing Netlify's own ad badge). A line in a wording refusedByDesign names is never set aside here: this pattern's netlify matches the site's own address on every Netlify page, so the badge's refused inline script is judged, and counted, by refusedByDesign alone (597b's second deployed run, 2026-11-14).

refusedByDesign.name: Netlify's own badge script
lines: ^Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src
^Refused to execute a script because its hash, its nonce, or 'unsafe-inline' does not appear in the script-src directive of the Content Security Policy\.
refusedByDesign.why: Netlify appends a loader after every page's own </html>, <script async src="/.netlify/scripts/hud?variant=public" data-nf-variant="public" ...>, a file of the site's own origin that 'self' lets run; it builds iframe#nl-badge-frame and writes the badge into its srcdoc with one inline script, which the policy scripts/netlify_badge.py writes refuses because it leaves 'unsafe-inline' out (documentation/07, Suppressing Netlify's own ad badge; #625 settled the frame, at about:srcdoc:85). Seen on both deployed runs (2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14) on each of the 11 pages in both engines, in the two wordings in `lines`, while the live policy listed exactly the site's own five inline scripts; the second run's served copy carried the loader after </html>, as a live test site's did with curl. Set aside only a message in these wordings said in `frame` (the console message's own address), on a page whose every document was read for `loader` (after its last </html>), and exactly refusalsPerDocument of them for each document that carried it (WebKit's two records of one message counted once): a refusal said in the page itself is the site's and fails, so a policy that lost one of the site's hashes is still red, and a second refusal in the frame, or one fewer, fails the page and names the count. The first version of this rule looked for the refused script in the page's own HTML and set nothing aside on real Netlify (the second run: 2 FAIL, 6 EXPECTED where 8 were predicted), because the script is built in the frame at run time. Each engine then says it in one EXPECTED line of the clean-page row, with each page's count, which verify-deploy.sh counts apart from thirdPartyHostsToday's: one an engine for each entry naming the host, on these hosts only (none when Netlify sent no badge).

engines.chromium: Chrome for Testing, the copy documentation/06 F7 installs (PLANTOIR_CHROME or --chrome), driven through Playwright's executablePath so it is the same binary as every other browser check.
engines.webkit: Playwright's WebKit build, the one playwright-core 1.63.0 pins (webkit-2359, WebKit 26.6 on this Mac), from browser-checks/fetch-browsers.sh's cache.

rows.name: katex

rows.name: graph

rows.name: python

rows.name: swift
rows.passes: Run pressed for real prints 42

rows.name: quiz

rows.name: tasks

rows.name: progress
rows.passes: My Progress, opened after that tick, reads 1 / 2 on the Tasks page's row

rows.name: geogebra
rows.passes: the file sketch opens on a real press: its canvas, from the site's own engine

rows.name: geogebra drag
rows.passes: point A dragged with real pointer events moves (#755)

rows.name: geogebra reset
rows.passes: GeoGebra's reset icon, pressed for real where geogebraFences.reset.icon puts it, puts A back where the sketch opened it (#792)

rows.name: geogebra keys
rows.passes: Shift+Tab and Space pressed again and again, the canvas focused before each, while the 150-line sketch's lines run: its points, counted after every press, never fall by more than one while the lines run (a reset getting in empties the construction, which the loader's marker repairs by the end, so the end alone cannot see it); all 150 are there at the end, and a press on its reset icon brings back all 150 (#792 item 12). Judged on its own sabotage only, which runs alone

rows.name: embeds
rows.passes: each YouTube, Vimeo, geogebra.org and PhET frame navigated to a document that answered 2xx (the frame's own response, never only a load event, which also fires on an error page), and no frame of the page refused to be shown (a Refused to display line, or the frame's document failing after it answered: a provider's X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors answers 200 and the engine blanks the frame, 597b review finding 1). Deployed sites only: the embeds need the network and nothing in them is the site's

rows.name: pdf
rows.passes: the handout's PDF link answers 200 with application/pdf

rows.name: print
rows.passes: on screen, every answer folded away; then Print pressed for real and a way of printing chosen: the print layout laid out at least one page, the diagram drawn on it, and the handout's Latin Modern face loaded (judged by its FontFace status)

rows.name: copy
rows.passes: the text block's copy button, pressed by a real pointer at its centre, is what the pointer hits and writes the block's text (#759; WebKit is where it was found). Read through a spy on navigator.clipboard.writeText, since WebKit refuses readText and has no clipboard permission to grant

rows.name: heading anchor
rows.passes: loaded with #test-of-success under eight runnable blocks: once they and the page's height have settled, the window is moved 400 px by a script (as the sidebar's own scroll to its entry moves it, #604) and 1,500 px more arrive above the heading (as a late diagram, picture or editor does over a real network). On this Mac every piece arrives before the page is shown, and WebKit keeps a fragment in view by itself until a script scrolls, so without these nothing would move and the row would pass with the site's landing gone (measured 2026-11-13). Then the heading must be in the top third of the window. WebKit has no scroll anchoring of its own; Chromium's is switched off, the imitation heading_anchor.mjs has always used

rows.name: fonts
rows.passes: the first family of each of the theme's three font settings that is not one of the device's own has at least one face whose status is loaded (not every face: display=swap loads only the weights the text uses)

rows.name: clean page
rows.passes: no console error and no page error but the expected lines for the host, no request refused by a policy (Chromium: a blocked request; WebKit: its Refused to line), no mixed content. On the Embeds page, what a teacher's embed says from inside its own frame (a console line about something it asked for, an error its own script threw, a request of its own that failed: measured 2026-11-13, YouTube's adverts, Vimeo's and PhET's fullscreen checks, GeoGebra reaching for the page) is set aside and counted in the row's own line, since the embeds row judges the frames. With no network to a host the site still asks (Google's fonts, cdnjs's Mermaid until #566), what that host's absence makes the page say is set aside, and the row says so

rows.name: own host
rows.passes: every request the page, its frames and its dedicated workers made, until it is scrolled to its end and has asked for nothing for a second (and at least 5 s after it loaded), went to the site's host or (on this Mac only; on a deployed site each is an EXPECTED line, see thirdPartyHostsToday) to one of thirdPartyHostsToday, and the page opened no frame on another host (only the Embeds page may, and only on the embeds row's allowedFrames, implementation review H1). Seen through the context's own router (WebKit hands a worker's requests to no page or context listener; #597 review H1), a WebSocket from the page through routeWebSocket, and a WebSocket from a dedicated worker through a watch put in front of the worker's script. A shared or service worker fails the row by being started at all: neither engine shows the router a shared worker's requests, nor WebKit a service worker's (implementation review M1, measured). WebRTC fails the row by being started (its STUN and TURN servers are asked over UDP, which no router sees). A sound or film asked of another host is recorded before it is refused. A WebSocket from a module a module worker imports is caught by the watch, imported first. Not seen, and said in the row's own line: a WebSocket from a worker made from a blob: or data: address (the site's policy refuses those workers on a published site, which the clean-page row sees), and anything asked for after the quiet period

rows.name: cold visit
rows.passes: five cold visits to the isolated Python page, each in a new context: fails when two or more take over 3 s to first contentful paint or the median does; one slow sample earns one counted retry (#625; read from performance paint entries, never a screenshot, which stays blank in headless WebKit until load). On a deployed site, two more routes the same way, the two of #625's sightings, each pressed for real on a link the check adds at the window's corner so the site's own router takes it: from the section's front page into the Python page (a full document navigation into isolation, measured 5 of 5) and from the Python page into the isolated Swift page (the router swaps it in, 5 of 5); paint is the new document's paint entry, or, for the router, the moment the target's title is in the article

sabotages.whyGateEngines: Measured 2026-11-13, one engine at a time with nothing else running: Chromium red 50 of 50 (10 of them beside twelve busy processes) and its unbroken row green 50 of 50; WebKit red only 46 of 50 (38 of 40, and 8 of 10 under load), because in some runs its Shift+Tab never reaches GeoGebra's reset icon and the lines run untouched, which nothing the page shows can tell from the hold working. A sabotage that passes 1 time in 12 would fail the gate at random. WebKit's unbroken row was green 50 of 50, so the row itself runs in both engines.
